title: The Weil cocycle yields a recurrence on compact-support endomorphisms
statement:
Fix a prime $p$, integers $a,n\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and its fixed algebraic closure $k$, and a prime $\ell\ne p$. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in the chosen algebraic closure, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and write $a_X:X\to s$. Use $D^b_c(X,A)$ and the compact-support functor $H(M)=R\Gamma_c(X,M)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(Ra_{X!}M)$ of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Put $\gamma=(z\mapsto z^q)^{-1}$, $g=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ and $h=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ as in [def-trf-scheme-frobenius], and $P_r=L(g^r)^*$, $T=P_1$, with derived pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Fix one compactification $c_0=(X_0\hookrightarrow\overline X_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0)$ of $a_{X_0}$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], and use its base change $c$ to represent $Ra_{X!}$ for every power.

For every $r\geq1$ let $\tau^{(r)}_{c,M}:H(M)\to H(P_rM)$ be the specified direct compact-support transport of [lem-trf-compact-frobenius-transport-composition]: the point transport along $h^r$ followed by the point fiber of the compactification exchange for the $r$-th-power square, using this same $c_0$. Write $\tau_{c,M}=\tau^{(1)}_{c,M}$ for the degree-one transport of [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport].

Let $(K,\varphi)\in D^b_{ctf,\mathrm W}(X,A)$ be a strict Weil complex [def-trf-strict-weil-complex], with $\varphi:TK\xrightarrow{\sim}K$, and use the specified iterates $\varphi^{[r]}:P_rK\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ of [def-trf-iterated-weil-map]. Define endomorphisms of the compact-support coefficient complex by
$$U_r=H(\varphi^{[r]})\circ\tau^{(r)}_{c,K}\quad(r\geq1).$$
Then $U_1=H(\varphi)\circ\tau_{c,K}$ and, for every $r\geq1$,
$$U_{r+1}=U_1\circ U_r.$$
The equality is an equality of morphisms of the compact-support derived coefficient complex, before applying a cohomology functor, with the actual direct transports from the retained compactification, rather than transports defined by repeated degree-one composition.

proof.text: By [def-trf-iterated-weil-map], the one-factor iterate is $\varphi^{[1]}=\varphi$. By [lem-trf-compact-frobenius-transport-composition], $\tau^{(1)}_{c,K}=\tau_{c,K}$. Substitution into the definition of $U_1$ gives $U_1=H(\varphi)\circ\tau_{c,K}$.

source.place: Compact-description proof, application of the iterated Weil map; explicit coefficient-complex calculation in FrobeniusOperatorCompactDescription.lean, docstring paragraph (4).

proof.text: Fix $r\geq1$. Let $b_{r,M}:TP_rM\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{r+1}M$ be the map denoted $c_{r,M}$ in [lem-trf-compact-frobenius-transport-composition], the inverse of the specified pullback-composition comparison. Apply that lemma at $M=K$ and $m=r$, with the retained $c_0$ of this statement. It gives $\tau^{(r+1)}_{c,K}=H(b_{r,K})\circ\tau^{(1)}_{c,P_rK}\circ\tau^{(r)}_{c,K}$. These are the direct transports for the power squares, all formed from this same compactification.

source.place: Compact-description proof, application of the iterated Weil map; explicit coefficient-complex calculation in FrobeniusOperatorCompactDescription.lean, docstring paragraph (4).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-iterated-weil-cocycle] with its indices $(m,n)=(1,r)$. Its canonical pullback identification is precisely $b_{r,K}:TP_rK\to P_{r+1}K$ from step 2. Since $\varphi^{[1]}=\varphi$, the cocycle, written with this identification rather than suppressing it, is $\varphi^{[r+1]}\circ b_{r,K}=\varphi\circ T(\varphi^{[r]})$ as maps $TP_rK\to K$. Both indices satisfy the lemma's positivity hypothesis.

source.place: Compact-description proof, application of the iterated Weil map; explicit coefficient-complex calculation in FrobeniusOperatorCompactDescription.lean, docstring paragraph (4).

proof.text: Put $u=\varphi^{[r]}:P_rK\to K$. Degree-one compact transport is natural in its coefficient complex by [def-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport]. At this morphism the naturality square reads $H(Tu)\circ\tau^{(1)}_{c,P_rK}=\tau^{(1)}_{c,K}\circ H(u)$. Here both objects lie in $D^b_c(X,A)$: $K$ does by hypothesis and $P_rK$ is isomorphic to $K$ via $u$. This is naturality of the specified transport with the fixed compactification.

source.place: Compact-description proof, application of the iterated Weil map; explicit coefficient-complex calculation in FrobeniusOperatorCompactDescription.lean, docstring paragraph (4).

proof.text: Using steps 2, 3 and 4 in that order, functoriality of $H$ and associativity give $$\begin{aligned}U_{r+1}&=H(\varphi^{[r+1]})\circ H(b_{r,K})\circ\tau^{(1)}_{c,P_rK}\circ\tau^{(r)}_{c,K}\\&=H(\varphi)\circ H(Tu)\circ\tau^{(1)}_{c,P_rK}\circ\tau^{(r)}_{c,K}\\&=H(\varphi)\circ\tau^{(1)}_{c,K}\circ H(u)\circ\tau^{(r)}_{c,K}\\&=U_1\circ U_r.\end{aligned}$$ Every arrow is a morphism of the compact-support derived coefficient complex; no cohomology functor has been applied. As $r\geq1$ was arbitrary, this proves the required recurrence for the actual direct transports.
